review_notes: I read the whole file and the Mathlib `Algebra/Homology/ShortComplex/Pushout.lean` and `Pullback.lean`. I grepped Mathlib for other pushout or pullback constructions on short complexes and found none beyond a snake-lemma-internal one. I grepped TauCeti/CategoryTheory for uses of `cobaseChange`, `baseChange` and `shortExact_cobaseChange`. The file's `IsPushout`/`IsPullback`-parameterised API is more general than Mathlib's `push`/`pull`, which use the chosen `pushout`/`pullback`. The callers in `Stable/Cone.lean` and `ExtensionClosed.lean` use arbitrary squares, so I would not remove the file's definitions. The remaining case for consolidation is the missing link to `push`/`pull`, which makes it a low-to-moderate-confidence finding. Mathlib's `push` and `pull` need `HasZeroMorphisms`, not `Preadditive`, so their hypotheses are compatible. I did not check whether `cobaseChange S (IsPushout.of_hasPushout _ _)` is defeq to `S.push u`. The other declarations (the composite and Noether results) have no Mathlib counterpart, because Mathlib has no exact-category theory.

findings.excerpt:
noncomputable def cobaseChangeπ (sq : IsPushout S.f u v w) : Q ⟶ S.X₃ :=
  sq.desc S.g 0 (by simp [S.zero])
findings.problem: Mathlib already has the short complex obtained by pushing out (resp. pulling back) a short complex along a morphism: `ShortComplex.push` is `Y ⟶ pushout S.f f ⟶ S.X₃` with `g := pushout.desc S.g 0 _`, and `ShortComplex.pull` is the dual. `cobaseChange` and `baseChange` define the same short complex with `desc S.g 0` / `lift S.f 0`, but for an arbitrary `IsPushout`/`IsPullback` square. The file never mentions `ShortComplex.push` or `ShortComplex.pull`. It does not relate its constructions to them, and it has its own `inl_cobaseChangeπ`, `baseChangeι_fst`, `_X₁`, `_f` and similar lemmas. Mathlib has also proved `ShortComplex.ShortExact.push` and `.pull` for abelian categories, and `TauCeti/CategoryTheory/Exact/Abelian.lean` has a separate `shortExact_cobaseChange`. The result is two parallel APIs for one construction, with no bridge between them. Exact-category users who start from `S.push u` cannot apply `conflation_cobaseChange` without re-deriving the square.
findings.proposed_change: Keep the square-parametrised definitions, since the callers in Stable/Cone.lean and ExtensionClosed.lean need arbitrary squares. Add a bridge: state that `cobaseChange S (IsPushout.of_hasPushout S.f u)` equals (or is canonically isomorphic to) `S.push u`, and likewise for `baseChange` and `S.pull`. Add `E.Conflation (S.push u)` and `E.Conflation (S.pull u)` corollaries of `conflation_cobaseChange` and `conflation_baseChange`. Use these in `exists_conflation_comp` and `exists_conflation_comp'`, which already use `pushout.inl` and `pullback.fst`. Alternatively, define the canonical case as `S.push` and note in the docstring why the general-square version is needed.
findings.benefit: Users of Mathlib's `ShortComplex.push` and `ShortComplex.pull` can reuse the conflation results directly. The two constructions are connected by an explicit lemma instead of silently duplicating each other. The duplicated `X₁`/`X₂`/`f`/`g` simp lemmas are tied to Mathlib's `@[simps]` ones.
